{{DISPLAYTITLE:Busemann ''G''-space}}
In [[mathematics]], a '''Busemann ''G''-space''' is a type of [[metric space]] first described by [[Herbert Busemann]] in 1942.

If <math>(X,d)</math> is a metric space such that

#  for every two distinct <math>x, y \in X</math> there exists <math>z \in X\setminus\{x,y\}</math> such that <math>d(x,z)+d(y,z)=d(x,y)</math> ([[Menger convexity]])
# every <math>d</math>-bounded set of infinite cardinality possesses [[accumulation point]]s
# for every <math>w \in X</math> there exists <math>\rho_w</math> such that for any distinct points <math>x,y \in B(w,\rho_w)</math> there exists <math>z \in  ( B(w,\rho_w)\setminus\{ x,y \} )^\circ</math> such that <math>d(x,y)+d(y,z)=d(x,z)</math> ([[geodesic]]s are locally extendable)
# for any distinct points <math>x,y \in X</math>, if <math>u,v \in X</math> such that <math>d(x,y)+d(y,u)=d(x,u)</math>, <math>d(x,y)+d(y,v)=d(x,v)</math> and <math>d(y,u)=d(y,v)</math>, then <math>u=v</math> (geodesic extensions are unique).

then ''X'' is said to be a ''Busemann'' ''G''-''space''.  Every Busemann ''G''-space is a [[homogeneous space]].

The [[Busemann conjecture]] states that every Busemann ''G''-space is a [[topological manifold]]. It is a special case of the [[Bing–Borsuk conjecture]]. The Busemann conjecture is known to be true for dimensions 1 to 4.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=M.|first1=Halverson, Denise|last2=Dušan|first2=Repovš|title=The Bing–Borsuk and the Busemann conjectures|journal=Mathematical Communications|date=23 December 2008|volume=13|issue=2|arxiv=0811.0886|url=https://hrcak.srce.hr/30884|language=en|issn=1331-0623}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|last1=Papadopoulos|first1=Athanase|title=Metric Spaces, Convexity and Nonpositive Curvature|date=2005|publisher=European Mathematical Society|isbn=9783037190104|pages=77|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=JrwzXZB0YrIC&pg=PA77|language=en}}</ref>
